subject: maths
title: Year 6 Multiplying and Dividing Larger Numbers
seo_title: Year 6 Multiplying and Dividing Larger Numbers: Free Maths Worksheets with Answer Key (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving natural and rational numbers and percentages, including in financial contexts; formulate the problems, choosing efficient calculation strategies and using digital tools where appropriate; interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation, justifying choices made
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on multiplying and dividing larger numbers, aligned to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M6N09): the area model and long multiplication, short and long division, what to do with a remainder, choosing the operation, and multi-step problems about school camp, fundraising and road trips. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Multiply by the ones, then by the tens with a place-holder zero. Divide from the left, then decide what the remainder means.
key_sub: 243 × 36 = 1458 + 7290 = 8748. 250 students, 48 seats a bus: 250 ÷ 48 = 5 r 10, so round up to 6 buses.
body_html:
The big idea

To multiply by a 2-digit number, split it into tens and ones. Multiply by each part, then add. To divide, work from the left and ask “how many groups fit?” at each step. In a word problem, decide first: are you putting equal groups together (multiply) or splitting a total into equal groups (divide)?

Multiplying: the area model

Multiplying: long multiplication

Long multiplication is the same idea in columns. Row 1 multiplies by the ones. Row 2 multiplies by the tens, so it starts with a place-holder zero (green).

Dividing by a 2-digit number: long division

Check with the inverse

9542 ÷ 23 = 414 r 20. Is it right?

Multiply the quotient by the divisor, then add the remainder: 414 × 23 = 9522 and 9522 + 20 = 9542.

Answer: Yes

What does the remainder mean?

The question asksDo this250 students, 48 seats a bus: 250 ÷ 48 = 5 r 10
How many are needed for everyone?Round up6 buses
How many are full?Round down5 full buses
How many are left over?The remainder is the answer10 students

When the amount can be split, such as money or a length, share the remainder too: $347 ÷ 4 = 86 r 3, and $3 ÷ 4 = 75c, so each share is $86.75 (not $86.30). As a fraction, 347 ÷ 4 = 86 34.

Choose the operation

The words sayOperationExample
equal groups, “each”, “times as many”Multiply36 boxes of 24 pens: 36 × 24
share equally, “groups of”, “how many times as many”Divide864 pens in boxes of 24: 864 ÷ 24

Multi-step problems need two or more steps. Write each step and its answer before you go on, and estimate to check the final answer makes sense.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
No place-holder zero (243 × 36 = 1458 + 729)Row 2 is × 30, so write 0 first: 7290
Forgetting a regrouped digitWrite it small and add it after you multiply
Missing a zero in the quotient (6216 ÷ 3 = 272)If the divisor does not go in, write 0: 2072
Writing r 3 as .3 ($347 ÷ 4 = $86.30)r 3 means 3 out of 4: 34 = 0.75, so $86.75
Rounding the wrong way (5 buses for 250 students)Ask: does everyone need a place? Then round up to 6
The wrong operation (864 pens in boxes of 24: 864 × 24)Grouping a total is division: 864 ÷ 24 = 36

faq.q: What multiplication and division do Year 6 students learn in Australia?
faq.a: Year 6 students solve practical problems with larger whole numbers, such as 3- and 4-digit numbers × 2-digit numbers and division by 1- and 2-digit numbers. They choose efficient strategies and explain what the answer, including any remainder, means in the situation (AC9M6N09).

faq.q: Why do you put a zero in the second row of long multiplication?
faq.a: In 243 × 36 the 3 means 3 tens, so row 2 is 243 × 30, not 243 × 3. The place-holder zero makes the row 7290 instead of 729.

faq.q: How do you know whether to round a remainder up or down?
faq.a: Round up when everyone or everything needs a place, such as buses or boxes to hold all the items. Round down when the question asks how many full groups you can make or how many you can afford.
No. NAPLAN is held in Years 3, 5, 7 and 9. Practising multi-step multiplication and division problems in Year 6 is good preparation for high school and the Year 7 numeracy test.

sets.title: 3- and 4-digit numbers × 2-digit numbers: area model and long multiplication

items.q: Use long multiplication.
Use the area model to find 529 × 53.
Use long multiplication to work out 978 × 89.
Use long multiplication.
Which is the best estimate for 5876 × 69?
items.e: Round each number: 5876 is about 6000 and 69 is about 70. 6000 × 70 = 420 000. The exact answer, 405 444, is close to it.

items.q: This area model shows 929 × 93. What number goes in the part marked ?
items.e: This part is 20 × 90. Use the fact 2 × 9 = 18, then write 2 zeros: 20 × 90 = 1800.

items.q: Use long multiplication to work out 105 × 82.
Use the area model to find 547 × 27.
Use long multiplication to work out 647 × 45.
Use long multiplication to work out 4353 × 56.
Use long multiplication to work out 7955 × 85.
What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Row 2 multiplies by the tens digit, so it is 6858 × 20. Write the place-holder 0 first, then 6858 × 2: 8 × 2 = 16, write 6, regroup 1; 5 × 2 + 1 = 11, write 1, regroup 1; 8 × 2 + 1 = 17, write 7, regroup 1; 6 × 2 + 1 = 13, write 13. The row is 137 160, not 13 716. Check: 54 864 + 137 160 = 192 024.

items.q: Use long multiplication.
Use long multiplication.
What number goes in the dashed box?
items.e: Row 2 multiplies by the tens digit, so it is 233 × 70. Write the place-holder 0 first, then 233 × 7: 3 × 7 = 21, write 1, regroup 2; 3 × 7 + 2 = 23, write 3, regroup 2; 2 × 7 + 2 = 16, write 16. The row is 16 310, not 1631. Check: 1398 + 16 310 = 17 708.

items.q: Jack worked out 536 × 75 like this. What mistake did he make?
items.e: Row 2 multiplies by 7 tens, so it must start with a place-holder 0: 536 × 70 = 37 520, not 3752. The answer is 2680 + 37 520 = 40 200.

items.q: Leo worked out 165 × 56 like this. What mistake did he make?
items.e: Row 1 should be 165 × 6 = 990 (5 × 6 = 30, write 0, regroup 3; 6 × 6 + 3 = 39, write 9, regroup 3; 1 × 6 + 3 = 9, write 9). Leo did not add the regrouped digits, so row 1 says 660. The answer is 990 + 8250 = 9240.

items.q: This area model shows 632 × 64. What number goes in the part marked ?
items.e: This part is 600 × 60. Use the fact 6 × 6 = 36, then write 3 zeros: 600 × 60 = 36 000.

items.q: Use long multiplication.
Use the area model to find 869 × 93.

sets.title: Dividing by 1- and 2-digit numbers: short and long division

items.q: Use long division.
Use long division to work out 6444 ÷ 36.
Use short division to work out 4407 ÷ 3.
items.e: 4 ÷ 3 = 1 r 1, carry the 1 to make 14; 14 ÷ 3 = 4 r 2, carry the 2 to make 20; 20 ÷ 3 = 6 r 2, carry the 2 to make 27; 27 ÷ 3 = 9. Answer: 1469. Check: 1469 × 3 = 4407.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 11 905 ÷ 42?
items.e: Round to numbers that divide easily: 11 905 is about 12 000 and 42 is about 40. 12 000 ÷ 40 = 300. The exact answer is 283 r 19.

items.q: Grace works out 3885 ÷ 37 = 15. What mistake did she make?
items.e: Check: 15 × 37 = 555, not 3885. When 37 does not go into the number, write 0 in the quotient. 3 is less than 37, so start with 38. 38 ÷ 37 = 1: 1 × 37 = 37, 38 − 37 = 1. Bring down 8 to make 18: 37 does not go into 18, so write 0 in the quotient. Bring down 5 to make 185: 185 ÷ 37 = 5: 5 × 37 = 185, 185 − 185 = 0. Answer: 105. Check: 105 × 37 = 3885.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 6025 ÷ 32?
items.e: Round to numbers that divide easily: 6025 is about 6000 and 32 is about 30. 6000 ÷ 30 = 200. The exact answer is 188 r 9.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 4 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 20; 20 ÷ 4 = 5; 4 does not go into 1, so write 0 in the quotient and carry the 1 to make 11; 11 ÷ 4 = 2 r 3. Answer: 502 r 3. Check: 502 × 4 + 3 = 2011.

items.q: Use long division.
Mei works out 4028 ÷ 21 = 190 r 38. What mistake did she make?
items.e: A remainder must be less than the divisor. 38 is more than 21, so 21 goes in once more: 38 − 21 = 17. The answer is 191 r 17. Check: 191 × 21 + 17 = 4028.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 4 ÷ 4 = 1; 4 does not go into 1, so write 0 in the quotient and carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 4 = 4 r 3, carry the 3 to make 36; 36 ÷ 4 = 9. Answer: 1049. Check: 1049 × 4 = 4196.

items.q: Use short division to work out 1967 ÷ 8.
items.e: 8 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 8 = 2 r 3, carry the 3 to make 36; 36 ÷ 8 = 4 r 4, carry the 4 to make 47; 47 ÷ 8 = 5 r 7. Answer: 245 r 7. Check: 245 × 8 + 7 = 1967.

items.q: Use long division to work out 805 ÷ 35.
1152 ÷ 9 = 128. Which calculation checks this answer?
items.e: Multiplication is the inverse of division: 128 × 9 = 1152, so the answer is right.

items.q: Use long division to work out 1611 ÷ 21.
items.e: 16 is less than 21, so start with 161. 161 ÷ 21 = 7: 7 × 21 = 147, 161 − 147 = 14. Bring down 1 to make 141: 141 ÷ 21 = 6: 6 × 21 = 126, 141 − 126 = 15. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 15. Answer: 76 r 15. Check: 76 × 21 + 15 = 1611.

items.q: Use short division.
items.e: 3 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 23; 23 ÷ 3 = 7 r 2, carry the 2 to make 25; 25 ÷ 3 = 8 r 1, carry the 1 to make 15; 15 ÷ 3 = 5. Answer: 785. Check: 785 × 3 = 2355.

items.q: Use long division.
items.e: 3 is less than 26, so start with 37. 37 ÷ 26 = 1: 1 × 26 = 26, 37 − 26 = 11. Bring down 6 to make 116: 116 ÷ 26 = 4: 4 × 26 = 104, 116 − 104 = 12. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 12. Answer: 14 r 12. Check: 14 × 26 + 12 = 376.

items.q: Ruby works out 1224 ÷ 6 = 24. What mistake did she make?
items.e: Check: 24 × 6 = 144, not 1224. When 6 does not go into the number, write 0 in the quotient. 6 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 12; 12 ÷ 6 = 2; 6 does not go into 2, so write 0 in the quotient and carry the 2 to make 24; 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Answer: 204. Check: 204 × 6 = 1224.

items.q: What is the remainder when 9274 is divided by 24?
items.e: The question asks for the remainder, not the quotient. 9 is less than 24, so start with 92. 92 ÷ 24 = 3: 3 × 24 = 72, 92 − 72 = 20. Bring down 7 to make 207: 207 ÷ 24 = 8: 8 × 24 = 192, 207 − 192 = 15. Bring down 4 to make 154: 154 ÷ 24 = 6: 6 × 24 = 144, 154 − 144 = 10. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 10. Answer: 386 r 10. Check: 386 × 24 + 10 = 9274.

items.q: Use long division to work out 605 ÷ 19.
items.e: 6 is less than 19, so start with 60. 60 ÷ 19 = 3: 3 × 19 = 57, 60 − 57 = 3. Bring down 5 to make 35: 35 ÷ 19 = 1: 1 × 19 = 19, 35 − 19 = 16. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 16. Answer: 31 r 16. Check: 31 × 19 + 16 = 605.

items.q: 9654 ÷ 38 = 254 r 2. Which calculation checks this answer?
items.e: Multiply the quotient by the divisor, then add the remainder: 254 × 38 = 9652 and 9652 + 2 = 9654.

sets.title: What does the remainder mean? Round up, round down, fraction or decimal

items.q: A school needs 844 exercise books for next year. They come in boxes of 48. How many boxes must the school order?
items.e: 844 ÷ 48 = 17 r 28. 17 boxes hold 17 × 48 = 816 books. The school still needs 28 more books, so it must order 1 more box: 18 boxes. Round up.

items.q: A farm has 958 eggs. It packs them into trays of 36. How many full trays can it pack?
items.e: 958 ÷ 36 = 26 r 22. The 22 eggs left over are not enough to fill another tray, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 26 trays.

items.q: The Year 6 class raised $786 at a cake stall. It is shared equally between 4 charities. How much does each charity get?
items.e: 786 ÷ 4 = 196 r 2. Dollars can be shared as cents, so share the $2 left over: $2 ÷ 4 = 50c. Each share is $196.50, not $196.20.

items.q: 8 friends share a $124 prize from the school art show equally. How much does each friend get?
items.e: 124 ÷ 8 = 15 r 4. Dollars can be shared as cents, so share the $4 left over: $4 ÷ 8 = 50c. Each share is $15.50, not $15.40.

items.q: 589 students line up in rows of 24 for the school photo. How many students are in the last row, which is not full?
items.e: 589 ÷ 24 = 24 r 13. The question asks how many are left over, so the remainder is the answer: 13 students.

items.q: Work out 101 ÷ 8. Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 8 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 10; 10 ÷ 8 = 1 r 2, carry the 2 to make 21; 21 ÷ 8 = 2 r 5. So the quotient is 12 r 5. The remainder 5 is 5 out of 8, so it is 58. Answer: 12 58.

items.q: A coach shares 383 tennis balls equally between 14 schools. Each school gets as many as possible. How many balls are left over?
items.e: 383 ÷ 14 = 27 r 5. The question asks how many are left over, so the remainder is the answer: 5 balls.

items.q: 255 students and teachers are going to the Year 6 camp. Each coach has 57 seats. How many coaches are needed?
items.e: 255 ÷ 57 = 4 r 27. 4 coaches hold 4 × 57 = 228 people. 27 people still need a place, so you need 1 more: 5 coaches. Round up.

items.q: A nursery has 683 seedlings. It plants them in trays of 32. 683 ÷ 32 = 21 r 11. To find how many trays are full, what should you do with the remainder?
items.e: A tray with fewer than 32 seedlings is not full, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 21 full trays.

items.q: A bakery makes 365 lamingtons. Each box holds 16 lamingtons. How many boxes can be filled?
items.e: 365 ÷ 16 = 22 r 13. The 13 lamingtons left over are not enough to fill another box, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 22 boxes.

items.q: Work out 107 ÷ 12. Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 10 is less than 12, so start with 107. 107 ÷ 12 = 8: 8 × 12 = 96, 107 − 96 = 11. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 11. So the quotient is 8 r 11. The remainder 11 is 11 out of 12, so it is 1112. Answer: 8 1112.

items.q: 4 friends split a $115 restaurant bill equally. 115 ÷ 4 = 28 r 3. To find how much each person pays, what should you do with the remainder?
items.e: Money can be split into cents, so the left-over dollars are shared too. Each person pays $28.75.

items.q: 289 students sign up for the summer cricket competition. Each team needs exactly 11 players. How many full teams can be made?
items.e: 289 ÷ 11 = 26 r 3. The 3 students left over are not enough to make another team, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 26 teams.

items.q: Work out 251 ÷ 7. Give your answer as a mixed numeral.
items.e: 7 does not go into 2, so carry the 2 to make 25; 25 ÷ 7 = 3 r 4, carry the 4 to make 41; 41 ÷ 7 = 5 r 6. So the quotient is 35 r 6. The remainder 6 is 6 out of 7, so it is 67. Answer: 35 67.

items.q: 361 students are going on a school excursion. Each bus has 42 seats. Mia works out 361 ÷ 42 = 8 r 25 and says 8 buses are needed. What is the right answer?
items.e: 8 buses only seat 8 × 42 = 336 students. The other 25 students still need seats, so Mia rounded the wrong way. Round up: 9 buses.

items.q: 163 Year 6 students are going to the swimming carnival. Each minibus has 12 seats for students. How many minibuses are needed?
items.e: 163 ÷ 12 = 13 r 7. 13 minibuses hold 13 × 12 = 156 students. 7 students still need a place, so you need 1 more: 14 minibuses. Round up.

items.q: A school has $892 to spend on new basketballs. Each basketball costs $38. How many basketballs can the school buy?
items.e: 892 ÷ 38 = 23 r 18. The $18 left over is not enough to buy another basketball, so ignore the remainder. Round down: 23 basketballs.

items.q: A family pays $302 for 20 nights at a caravan park. Each night costs the same. How much is one night?
items.e: 302 ÷ 20 = 15 r 2. Dollars can be shared as cents, so share the $2 left over: $2 ÷ 20 = 10c. Each share is $15.10, not $15.20.

items.q: 429 people are coming to the school musical. The chairs are set out in rows of 18. How many rows are needed so everyone has a seat?
items.e: 429 ÷ 18 = 23 r 15. 23 rows hold 23 × 18 = 414 people. 15 people still need a place, so you need 1 more: 24 rows. Round up.

items.q: 682 people are going to a footy final by bus. Each bus seats 57. 682 ÷ 57 = 11 r 55. To find how many buses are needed, what should you do with the remainder?
items.e: Everyone needs a seat, so the left-over people need 1 more bus. Round up: 12 buses.

sets.title: Choose the operation: multiply or divide?

items.q: An excursion to the aquarium costs $32 for each student. 74 students are going. What is the total cost?
items.e: Equal groups put together, so multiply. Row 1: 74 × 2 = 148. Row 2: 74 × 30 = 2220 (write the place-holder 0, then 74 × 3 = 222). Add: 148 + 2220 = 2368.

items.q: A vineyard has 199 rows of grapevines with 39 vines in each row. Which number sentence gives the number of vines?
items.e: Equal groups put together, so multiply: 199 × 39 = 7761.

items.q: A school orders 86 packs of paper. Each pack has 466 sheets. Jack works out 86 × 466 = 6524 sheets. What mistake did he make?
items.e: Multiplying is right, but the answer is too small: 86 × 466 is about 90 × 500 = 45 000. Row 1: 466 × 6 = 2796. Row 2: 466 × 80 = 37 280 (write the place-holder 0, then 466 × 8 = 3728). Add: 2796 + 37 280 = 40 076.

items.q: A 1624 km road trip is driven in 7 days, the same distance each day. How far is driven each day?
items.e: Share or group the total, so divide: 7 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 16; 16 ÷ 7 = 2 r 2, carry the 2 to make 22; 22 ÷ 7 = 3 r 1, carry the 1 to make 14; 14 ÷ 7 = 2. Answer: 232. Check: 232 × 7 = 1624.

items.q: A school pays $2125 for 25 new chairs. Each chair costs the same. Which number sentence gives the cost of one chair?
items.e: You know the total and the size of each group (or the number of groups), so divide. Put the total first: 2125 ÷ 25 = 85. 25 ÷ 2125 is the wrong way round.

items.q: A 476 m roll of fencing wire is cut into 17 equal pieces. Which number sentence gives the length of each piece?
items.e: You know the total and the size of each group (or the number of groups), so divide. Put the total first: 476 ÷ 17 = 28. 17 ÷ 476 is the wrong way round.

items.q: The P&C raises $2800 at the school fete. It shares the money equally between 16 classes. How much does each class get?
items.e: Share or group the total, so divide: 2 is less than 16, so start with 28. 28 ÷ 16 = 1: 1 × 16 = 16, 28 − 16 = 12. Bring down 0 to make 120: 120 ÷ 16 = 7: 7 × 16 = 112, 120 − 112 = 8. Bring down 0 to make 80: 80 ÷ 16 = 5: 5 × 16 = 80, 80 − 80 = 0. Answer: 175. Check: 175 × 16 = 2800.

items.q: 480 chocolates are packed into boxes of 32. Ava works out 480 × 32 = 15 360 boxes. What mistake did she make?
items.e: Packing a total into groups of 32 is division, not multiplication. 480 ÷ 32 = 15 boxes. 15 360 boxes is far more than the number of chocolates, so it cannot be right.

items.q: The canteen sold 313 sausage rolls in Term 1. It sold 4 times as many in the whole year. Which number sentence gives how many it sold in the whole year?
items.e: “4 times as many” means multiply: 313 × 4 = 1252.

items.q: Kai read 552 pages over the holidays. His brother read 138 pages. How many times as many pages did Kai read?
items.e: “How many times as many” means divide the bigger number by the smaller one: 552 ÷ 138 = 4. So Kai read 4 times as many pages. 552 − 138 = 414 finds how many more pages, not how many times as many.

items.q: A plane has 353 seats. 222 seats are taken. Which number sentence gives the number of empty seats?
items.e: Find the difference between all the seats and the taken seats, so subtract: 353 − 222 = 131.

items.q: 231 students sign up for summer cricket. They are put into equal teams of 11. How many teams are there?
items.e: Share or group the total, so divide: 2 is less than 11, so start with 23. 23 ÷ 11 = 2: 2 × 11 = 22, 23 − 22 = 1. Bring down 1 to make 11: 11 ÷ 11 = 1: 1 × 11 = 11, 11 − 11 = 0. Answer: 21. Check: 21 × 11 = 231.

items.q: 168 students are split into equal teams of 14. Which number sentence gives the number of teams?
items.e: You know the total and the size of each group (or the number of groups), so divide. Put the total first: 168 ÷ 14 = 12. 14 ÷ 168 is the wrong way round.

items.q: Noah runs laps of a 400 m track. How many laps must he run to cover 3200 m? Which number sentence gives the answer?
items.e: You know the total and the size of each group (or the number of groups), so divide. Put the total first: 3200 ÷ 400 = 8. 400 ÷ 3200 is the wrong way round.

items.q: 2822 people watch the first cricket match and 3162 people watch the second. Which number sentence gives how many people watched altogether?
items.e: Two different amounts are put together, so add: 2822 + 3162 = 5984.

items.q: A footy club pays $34 for each of its 19 players to go to a training camp. Isla works out the total cost as 34 ÷ 19 = 1 r 15. What mistake did she make?
items.e: Each player costs the same amount, so the total is equal groups put together: multiply. $34 × 19 = $646.

items.q: A school buys 147 boxes of pencils. Each box holds 48 pencils. How many pencils is that?
items.e: Equal groups put together, so multiply. Row 1: 147 × 8 = 1176. Row 2: 147 × 40 = 5880 (write the place-holder 0, then 147 × 4 = 588). Add: 1176 + 5880 = 7056.

items.q: A school buys 13 new netballs at $32 each. Which number sentence gives the total cost?
items.e: Equal groups put together, so multiply: 32 × 13 = 416.

items.q: The school hall has 18 rows of chairs with 23 chairs in each row. Which number sentence gives the number of chairs?
items.e: Equal groups put together, so multiply: 18 × 23 = 414.

items.q: 592 students are split into 16 equal groups for a science excursion. Leo works out 592 ÷ 16 = 37 students in each group. What mistake did he make?
items.e: Sharing the students equally into groups is division, and 37 × 16 = 592, so Leo is right.

sets.title: Multi-step problems: school camp, fundraising and road trips

items.q: Raffle tickets come in books of 25. The class sells 42 full books. Each ticket costs $3. How much money is raised?
126 students do swimming lessons in Term 4. Each student has 8 lessons, and each lesson costs $12. What is the total cost?
155 students go on an excursion. Each bus seats 45 students and costs $480 to hire. How much do the buses cost altogether?
items.e: Step 1: 155 ÷ 45 = 3 r 20, so round up: 4 buses. Step 2: 4 × $480 = $1920.

items.q: 6 friends go on a road trip. Fuel costs $371 and the cabin costs $451. They share the total cost equally. How much does each person pay?
A school fun run raises $1449 on Friday and $1075 on Saturday. The money is shared equally between 4 charities. How much does each charity get?
The canteen buys 21 boxes of juice with 24 bottles in each box. It sells all but 29 of the bottles for $2 each. How much money does it take?
A school buys 15 sets of readers at $265 a set. It pays from a budget of $5000. How much of the budget is left?
Ruby's family saves $95 a week for 32 weeks for a holiday. The holiday costs $2400. How much money is left over?

On camp, 64 students visit a wildlife park. Entry is $26 for each student, and the bus costs $896 for the group. The bus cost is shared equally between the students. How much does each student pay altogether?
items.e: Step 1: share the bus: $896 ÷ 64 = $14 each. Step 2: add the entry: $26 + $14 = $40.

items.q: A family's road trip is 3746 km long. They have already driven 1634 km. They drive the rest in 8 days, the same distance each day. How far do they drive each day?
items.e: Step 1: 3746 − 1634 = 2112 km left. Step 2: 2112 ÷ 8 = 264 km each day. Check: 264 × 8 = 2112.

items.q: On a road trip, a family fills the car 16 times at $98 each time and stays 13 nights at a caravan park at $58 a night. What is the total cost?
On a road trip, a family drives an average of 92 km each hour. They drive for 6 hours a day for 4 days. How far do they drive?
items.e: Step 1: one day: 92 × 6 = 552 km. Step 2: 4 days: 552 × 4 = 2208 km.

items.q: For a sausage sizzle, the P&C needs 334 sausages. Sausages come in packs of 30, and each pack costs $16. How much do the sausages cost?
items.e: Step 1: 334 ÷ 30 = 11 r 4, so round up: 12 packs. Step 2: 12 × $16 = $192.

items.q: 133 students and 9 teachers are going to camp. Each coach has 45 seats. How many coaches are needed?
items.e: Step 1: 133 + 9 = 142 people. Step 2: 142 ÷ 45 = 3 r 7. The 7 people left over still need seats, so round up: 4 coaches.

items.q: The Year 6 class sells 247 cupcakes at $3 each at a cake stall. The ingredients cost $185. How much money does the class make after paying for the ingredients?
items.e: Step 1: 247 × $3 = $741 taken. Step 2: subtract the cost: $741 − $185 = $556.

items.q: The school wants to raise $5000 for new library books. It raises $165 each week for 25 weeks. How much more does it still need?
items.e: Step 1: 25 × $165 = $4125 raised. Step 2: $5000 − $4125 = $875 still needed.

items.q: A school buys 120 laptops at $420 each. The laptops are shared equally between 6 classes. What is the value of the laptops each class gets?
The school garden club plants 29 rows of seedlings with 22 in each row. 43 seedlings do not survive. How many seedlings are left?
items.e: Step 1: 29 × 22 = 638 seedlings. Step 2: 638 − 43 = 595.

items.q: 141 students are going on camp. Each tent sleeps 6 students. Each tent costs $35 to hire. What is the cost of the tents?
items.e: Step 1: 141 ÷ 6 = 23 r 3, so round up: 24 tents. Step 2: 24 × $35 = $840.

items.q: Year 6 camp costs $185 for each student, plus $1680 to hire the coaches. 59 students are going. What is the total cost?
